text:
alice: quick follow-up from the kernel autotune RFC — thinking out loud about a complementary heuristic: "attn-span bucketing" for cold/short sequences rather than only seqlen buckets.

ben: curious — how do you define attn-span vs seqlen here?

alice: attn-span = max distance between non-padding tokens that meaningfully interact (approx last_nonpad_idx - first_nonpad_idx). Many user inputs are short but have scattered tokens (code, csv), so seqlen bucket alone overallocates kv cache.

carla: makes sense. So small seqlen but large attn-span -> kernel choice should prefer sparse attention path or different tiling?

alice: exactly. For Llama-like layers we can prefer chunked attention kernels when attn-span > X and seqlen < Y. This reduces KV cache pressure and avoids huge contiguous k/v tensors for mostly-empty prefixes.

ben: what's the heuristic threshold X/Y? static or learned?

dinesh: propose starting with simple thresholds: attn_span_ratio = attn_span / seqlen. If ratio > 0.6 and seqlen < 512 -> choose chunked/sparse kernel. We'll autotune ratio per model/hardware over time.

alice: +1. Also need to account for batching: heterogeneous batch shapes with mixed short and long sequences. Kernel switch cost matters. We should probe a candidate kernel only up to a budgeted number of samples per minute to avoid thrashing.

carla: how do we probe without impacting latency SLOs?

dinesh: do asynchronous micro-probing on low-priority nodes: spawn N synthetic requests that mirror recent traffic distribution (weights by seqlen/attn_span). Keep probing windows to <1% of capacity. If probe p50/p95 better by >5% and cost delta < threshold, mark candidate as preferred.

alice: infra-bot logs attached for earlier probe run (example):
```
# probe summary
model: redwood-open-13b
hw: gpus/v100-32
samples: 120
probe_budget_pct: 0.8
result: chunked_kernel +9% tokens/sec, +1.2ms p95 latency
```

ben: nice. We should also add a decay TTL for decisions so a kernel selected during peak traffic doesn't persist when workload changes. Maybe 15m sliding window + exponential decay.

carla: caching implications? If we switch kernels we may need to invalidate or migrate KV caches. That could be expensive.

alice: two options: (1) conservative: avoid kernel switches if active cache hit rate > H, (2) lazy-migrate: keep old kernel's kv around for TTL, cold-evict after no hits. We tested lazy-migrate in canary — small mem spike but fewer misses.

ben: how about policies in runtime config? Example YAML sketch: 
```
autotune:
  max_probe_per_min: 2
  probe_nodes: low_priority
  attn_span_ratio_threshold: 0.6
  seqlen_max_for_span: 512
  cache_safe_hit_pct: 0.75
  decision_ttl_secs: 900
```

carla: can we get metrics hooks to evaluate regressions automatically? E.g., per-route probe tags, kernel_switch_count, kv_migrated_bytes, probe_latency_delta.

dinesh: yes — add these to runtime telemetry and circuit-breaker rules. If kernel_switch_count spikes or kv_migrated_bytes > X in window -> rollback to baseline.

alice: rollout plan suggestion: 1) lab microbench + deterministic inputs 2) low-traffic region canary (1% routes) 3) traffic-shadow probe (no switching) 4) 10% gradual rollout with mem and latency alarms 5) full roll when stable.

ben: +1. For experiments, I'll put together the probe harness that synthesizes attn_span distributions from prod traces.

carla: also add an eval that checks output parity for chunked vs dense kernels for a sample of prompts to guard against numerical divergence.

alice: agreed. I'll open a short RFC follow-up with config defaults and the canary checklist. tagging @dinesh to help spec probe budget. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued: autotune-probe-harness/v2 on pool-lowprio (job id: 64281)

ben: thanks — will push the harness today and ping when probes start.

carla: ack. good set of next steps.
